methodology.name: Bot elimination and ticker extraction
methodology.what: Drops posts from accounts under 30 days old, with under 3 followers, posting more than 5 times a minute, or copy-pasting the same text. Finds tickers from cashtags, exchange tags and company names, limited to stocks listed on NYSE, Nasdaq and NYSE American, including ADRs of foreign companies such as TSMC or Alibaba.
details: Window: every post and article from the last 7 days is read. A week is long enough to collect a meaningful sample from StockTwits and news feeds, and short enough that the chatter is still about this week's events.

Bot rules (StockTwits only, news has no accounts): accounts younger than 30 days, with fewer than 3 followers, posting more than 5 times a minute, or posting the same text repeatedly are removed. These are the usual signs of spam and pump accounts.
Tickers are found from cashtags ($AAPL), exchange tags (NASDAQ: AAPL) and company names (Apple). Only US-listed common stocks, REITs and ADRs count; ETFs and over-the-counter names are excluded.
Each stock gets a chatter score that combines social posts and news articles, and a snapshot is saved every day so later runs can tell whether this week's chatter is unusual for that stock.

methodology.name: Market and volume hard filters
methodology.what: Requires market cap of at least $300M, price above $1, real trading liquidity and history; no SPACs. Chatter must be unusual (z-score), come from many different users (70%+ unique), and be confirmed by real trading volume. Fundamentals: positive P/E up to 60, growing revenue, debt/equity up to 200%.
details: Size and quality: market value of at least $300M, share price above $1, at least $5M traded per day, and at least 30 trading days in the last 3 months. Small, thinly traded stocks are the easiest to pump and dump. SPACs (blank-check companies) are excluded.
Enough chatter: at least 5 posts or independent articles.

Unusual chatter: a z-score of at least 1 (one standard deviation above normal). Once 3+ daily snapshots exist, each stock is compared with its own normal level; before that, with the other stocks this week.
Many voices: at least 70% of posts must come from different accounts, so a handful of users cannot push a stock onto the list.

Backed by real trading: the last 3 days' volume must be at least 80% of its usual level (the 20 days before), and a big chatter spike needs volume 1.2x normal. Talk without trading suggests artificial hype.
Fundamentals: profitable (positive P/E) with P/E up to 60, revenue not shrinking year on year, and debt/equity up to 200%. At least 2 of the 3 must be known.

methodology.name: Sentiment scoring
methodology.what: Normalises emojis and slang, isolates each ticker in multi-ticker posts, scores with FinBERT plus a trader-slang dictionary, one vote per user.
details: FinBERT is a language model trained on financial text. It reads each post or headline and scores it as positive, negative or neutral for the stock.
Trader slang and emojis ("to the moon", "bagholder", 🚀) are translated first, using a seed dictionary plus slang the system has learned from posts with Bullish/Bearish tags.
When a post mentions several stocks, only the part about each stock is scored for it.
One vote per user: a single account posting 20 times counts once.
The model is checked every run against traders' own Bullish/Bearish tags; that accuracy is shown in "How far to trust it".

methodology.name: AI catalyst and sarcasm review
methodology.what: An LLM explains why each stock is discussed and must cite real headlines. Hype, meme and spam driven interest, negative or minor catalysts are rejected; sarcastic posts are re-scored.
details: An AI model (LLM) reads the week's headlines for each remaining stock and names the catalyst: earnings, a deal, a product, an approval, and so on. It must link the real headlines it used.
Stocks are rejected when the catalyst is bad for the share price, too minor to matter, or when the interest looks driven by hype, memes or pump language rather than news.
Posts the sentiment model may have misread (sarcasm, jokes) are re-checked and re-scored.
Survivors are ranked by a score that combines sentiment, catalyst strength, unusual chatter and trading volume, each as a percentile against the other finalists.
If the AI review fails for a stock, that stock is not approved. Answers are cached to keep costs low.

methodology.name: Risk checks and diversification
methodology.what: Removes stocks that already jumped over 20% in 5 days, are very overbought or very volatile; flags earnings within 7 days and high short interest; max 2 per sector and no near-duplicates.
details: Chasing: a stock already up more than 20% in 5 trading days, or with RSI above 80 (very overbought), is removed. The chatter is probably reacting to a move that already happened.
Volatility: annualised 30-day volatility above 90% is removed; above 60% is flagged.
Flags shown on the pick: earnings within 7 days, short interest above 20% of the float, price more than 25% above its 50-day average or below its 200-day average, and a negative analyst consensus.
Different industries: at most 2 picks per sector, so a full Top 5 covers at least 3 industries whenever enough stocks qualify. The next-ranked stock from another sector takes the freed place.
No near-duplicates: two stocks whose daily returns moved almost identically over the last 120 sessions (correlation above 0.85) would be the same bet twice, so only the higher-ranked one is kept.
Track record: every pick is logged with its price and the S&P 500's, and its 5- and 20-day results are reported in later runs.
